text:
Sam Bennett already has two hat tricks this season, the second a natural one against Buffalo on Nov. 21, when he toe-dragged around Rasmus Dahlin for the first goal and, as Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic put it, "had way too much room to meander around Buffalo's zone" on another. The Conn Smythe winner from Florida's second straight Cup run is scoring like a first-line sniper: 11 goals in 25 games.

Our numbers think the goals are running ahead of him. He's shooting 18% against 13% last season, 3.4 goals above what his chances deserve, and the last ten games (7 goals) came on normal chance volume while his ice time dropped 1:30 a night. The process underneath is good, not great: Florida gets 55% of the expected goals at five on five with him on.

What hasn't changed is the job. Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best players (90th percentile competition) last season, and he still throws hits (53). His points pace sits right at the middle of our talent range, so the total is honest even if the goal share isn't. Our numbers expect some of those goals to turn back into near misses.
headline: Bennett's hat tricks and the cooling ahead
